carrier_name: Mutual of Omaha (United of Omaha Life Insurance Company)

must_contain: United of Omaha Life Insurance Company

extraction_notes:
This is a Mutual of Omaha (underwritten by United of Omaha Life Insurance Company) Voluntary Accident Insurance proposal. Unlike medical/dental quotes, this document has only ONE plan/class (Class 1: All Eligible Employees) rather than multiple plan tiers - do not expect multiple 'plans' unless the document explicitly shows multiple classes (e.g., Class 1, Class 2) with different benefit schedules or rates. If multiple classes ARE present, each class must get its own full benefits object pulled from its own section of the schedule.

Layout structure:
- Page 1: Header with proposal group name, effective date, and underwriting carrier. Then ELIGIBILITY section (class definitions, hours requirements, age termination, child eligibility) - these are plan metadata, not benefits. Then ACCIDENT INSURANCE section with coverage tiers/options and Express Benefit. Then ACCIDENT BENEFITS section begins with Initial Care & Emergency Benefits table (ER, Urgent Care, Physician Visit, Ground/Air Ambulance).
- Page 2-4: Specified Injury Benefits - large fracture/dislocation tables broken out by bone/joint group with Open Reduction and Closed Reduction dollar columns (do not need to record every single bone line item verbatim in the schema; can summarize as a range but note this is a large table with per-bone amounts). Also Other Injuries (lacerations, burns by TBSA %, dental care), Hospital/Surgical/Diagnostic Benefits table, Follow-Up Care Benefits table (physician visits, medical device, prosthetics, therapy), Additional Benefits table (transportation, lodging, childcare, health screening, child sports injury booster).
- Page 4 continued: CATASTROPHIC BENEFITS section - Principal Sum amounts by relationship (employee/spouse/child), then Accidental Death %, Common Carrier Accidental Death %, Transportation of Remains, Dismemberment & Paralysis benefits (all as % of principal sum), and Other Benefits (Reasonable Modifications, Coma).
- Page 4-5: ADDITIONAL BENEFITS AND FEATURES section - Open Enrollment, Annual Open Enrollment, Portability, Continuation for Temporary Layoff, Continuation for Leave of Absence, Continuation for Federal/State Laws - these are policy features, not benefit cost-shares, generally can be omitted from benefits map or noted briefly.
- Final page: PARTICIPATION AND PREMIUM STRUCTURE section with participation assumptions table, and ACCIDENT MONTHLY PREMIUM RATES table with four tiers: Employee/Member, Employee/Member + Spouse, Employee/Member + Child(ren), Employee/Member + Family. This is the rates table - map directly to employee_only/employee_spouse/employee_children/family schema fields. Also includes Rate Guarantee Period and Rate Guarantee Date.

Quirks: This is accident-only supplemental insurance, not major medical, so there is NO deductible, no OOP max, no coinsurance/network structure in the traditional sense - omit deductible/oop_max fields or leave blank. There's also an 'Alternate' rate quoted at top of page 1 (e.g. Alternate: 8.00) - this appears to be an alternate rate/plan option indicator worth noting if it recurs in future docs, may indicate a second plan design was proposed but only one rate schedule detail was included; flag this for review if it appears again since it may mean a second plan's premium rate exists elsewhere not fully detailed. Always check for multiple 'Class' definitions and multiple premium rows in the final rate table, as additional classes would require additional plan entries with their own full benefit schedules.
